title: Overlapping prepare/start requests on the support site can assign a candidate two Part 1 question sets
description: On the support site (TEAM unset), assignPart1Questions checks for an existing assignment with a separate SELECT and only then, after several more awaited D1 reads (ensurePerfSchema, part1_seen, four pickLeastUsed pool queries), inserts the chosen set with a plain INSERT batch. The support schema's only uniqueness rule on part1_assignments is PRIMARY KEY(candidate_id, question_id); there is no (candidate_id, position) constraint. A signed-in candidate can send overlapping POST /api/candidate/part1/prepare requests (no test-open gate; only a submitted check) or /part1/start requests (the normal page only calls start, at public/app.js:648, so the duplicate requires deliberate or accidental concurrent calls). If two requests both pass the existence check before either batch commits and their picks share no question id, both batches commit and the candidate holds 2N rows with duplicated positions. If any id overlaps, the later batch fails on the primary key and that request errors, so only fully disjoint picks produce the duplicate; disjointness needs at least 2x the per-category count at the least-used tier. Consequences source shows: /part1/start and /part1/questions return every assigned row, so the candidate sees twice the configured share of the question bank (more to pass to later candidates); gradeCandidate grades every assigned row (double OpenAI calls for that candidate); part1Summary and the CSV export's Total awarded/Total max sum every scored row, so the candidate's absolute awarded total can exceed what a normal candidate can reach (the max grows too, so a percentage view is not inflated in the same way); and question_usage gets +1 for N extra distinct questions, skewing the least-used rotation for later candidates. The writers path fixes this exact race with per-position NOT EXISTS inserts plus UNIQUE(candidate_id, position); the support code and migrations have neither. Whether the interleaving actually occurs under the Workers/D1 runtime was not executed in this run.
claimed_root_cause: src/lib/randomize.ts:31-62 is a non-atomic check-then-act: SELECT 1 FROM part1_assignments WHERE candidate_id = ? (lines 32-35), several awaited reads, then a separate env.DB.batch of plain INSERT INTO part1_assignments (candidate_id, question_id, position) VALUES (?, ?, ?) (lines 59-62). migrations/0001_init.sql:40-45 constrains only (candidate_id, question_id), and no later support migration (0002-0016) or runtime ensure* helper adds a (candidate_id, position) uniqueness rule, so a second set with disjoint question ids is accepted. The NOT EXISTS position guard (src/lib/randomize.ts:220-225) and UNIQUE INDEX idx_p1a_cand_pos (migrations-docs/0017_writers_indexes.sql:15, applied only via env.docs migrations_dir) exist only on the writers path.

trace.description: Reached by any signed-in candidate (requireCandidate at line 103; the global Origin guard at src/index.ts:20-23 allows requests without Origin). The only gate is the submitted check at line 145: no test-open gate, no lock. /part1/start (line 152) is a second entry with the open gate at line 157.
Calls assignPart1Questions(env, candidate.id); /part1/start calls it too at line 162.
The SELECT 1 existence check runs as its own statement and returns early only if a row already exists (line 35); overlapping requests that read before any batch commits all proceed.

Each request draws its own set ordered by usage with a random tie-break (randomize.ts:125-129); within an equal-usage tier at least twice the per-category count, overlapping requests can pick disjoint ids.

Plain INSERT batch at positions 0..N-1. A fully disjoint second set violates no constraint (PRIMARY KEY is (candidate_id, question_id) only) and commits beside the first; a partially overlapping set fails the whole batch instead.

questionsFor (candidate.ts:130-139) returns every part1_assignments row for the candidate, so all 2N questions are shown. gradeCandidate (src/routes/admin.ts:1424-1436) grades every assigned row, and the export totals (src/routes/admin.ts:1108) sum them.

evidence.description: part1_assignments has PRIMARY KEY (candidate_id, question_id) only; nothing bounds rows or positions per candidate. No support migration 0002-0016 and no runtime ensure* helper (src/lib/db.ts:149-172) adds a position constraint.
'if (existing) return; // idempotent' is the only guard, and it is not atomic with the INSERT batch at line 62.

The writers variant assignDocsPart1 documents this race ('two overlapping calls (prefetch + start) can't give one candidate two sets') and guards each insert with NOT EXISTS on (candidate_id, position) (lines 222-225).

UNIQUE INDEX idx_p1a_cand_pos ON part1_assignments(candidate_id, position) exists only in migrations-docs, which wrangler.toml applies only to env.docs (migrations_dir = "migrations-docs" at line 134; support uses "migrations" at line 23).

part1Summary sums ai_score (and max_marks at line 18) over every scored answer row with no per-candidate question cap, so a larger set raises the absolute awarded total shown in the export (src/routes/admin.ts:1108).

question_usage is incremented for each committed set's fresh questions, so a second disjoint set adds +1 use to N extra questions for one student and skews the least-used rotation for later candidates.
RL_CANDIDATE allows 120 requests per 60 s per cookie, which does not prevent a small burst of overlapping prepare calls.

blockers: no OS-enforced sandbox for target execution in this run

Whether concurrent Worker requests interleave against D1 so that both existence checks run before either INSERT batch commits must be observed by execution (miniflare D1 in vitest, or the deployed Worker and D1)

validation_plan.local: Add a vitest case in test/candidate.test.ts using test/helpers.ts (configPath ./wrangler.toml gives 2 SQL + 1 Python + 1 DSA + 1 Scenario = 5 per student). migrate(); seedCandidate('c1','c1@x.com','part2_ready'); do NOT rely on seedQuestions() alone (its 3 SQL / 2 per other category cannot yield disjoint sets): insert at least 10 active question_bank rows per category (sql, python, dsa, scenario) directly with env.DB, leaving question_usage empty. Get the cookie with candidateCookie('c1@x.com'). For 20 iterations: DELETE FROM part1_assignments, part1_seen and question_usage rows for c1/all questions; then Promise.all 8 req('/api/candidate/part1/prepare', { method: 'POST', headers: { Cookie: cookie, Origin: 'https://test.local' } }) (accept 200 or 500 per response, since an overlapping batch fails on the primary key); then read SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(DISTINCT position) AS p FROM part1_assignments WHERE candidate_id='c1'. The invariant fails if n > 5 in any iteration (and p < n shows duplicated positions). On a failing iteration, also POST /api/candidate/part1/start (after opening the test or with it open by default) and check questions.length > 5. Regression for the fix (per-position NOT EXISTS insert plus a UNIQUE(candidate_id, position) index in a new support migration): the same test must always yield n = 5 and p = 5.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed only, read-only, run by the owner on the support D1 (not audit traffic): SELECT candidate_id, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(DISTINCT position) AS p FROM part1_assignments GROUP BY candidate_id HAVING n > 5 OR p < n (replace 5 with the configured SQL+PYTHON+DSA+SCENARIO per-student total) to see whether any real candidate already holds a doubled set.

title: Anonymous API traffic can use up the account-wide daily Workers request and D1 write allowances; every in-Worker ceiling is per network
description: Both sites (talo and talo-docs) run on one Cloudflare account, and the repository's own budget assumes the Free plan's account-wide allowances: 100,000 Worker requests and 100,000 D1 rows written per day, reset at 00:00 UTC (docs/WRITERS-DATA-DESIGN.md:19-20, 42). Every request limit in the source is per network. RL_IP allows 3000 requests per minute per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 (wrangler.toml:42, 152) and is checked inside the Worker (src/index.ts:26-28), so a refused request is still a counted invocation. The candidate sign-in counter writes at least one D1 row per unlisted-email attempt, up to 200 per network per 10-minute window, on both sites; once a network is paused, further attempts cost one D1 read and no write. Nothing bounds the total across networks. With no credentials, one client at one IPv4 address can send about 100,000 /api/ requests in roughly 33 minutes. A client holding a routed IPv6 prefix can rotate /64s (about 500 networks x 200 attempts) to also drive about 100,000 rate_limits upserts; those same requests count against the request allowance, so the two allowances drain together. If the account is on the Free plan, both sites' API calls would then fail for every candidate in a live drive until 00:00 UTC (static pages still load). Honest framing: the amplification is 1:1 (one cheap request per unit of quota, possibly two rows written if the primary-key index is counted), this is sustained volume rather than a superlinear input, and it matters only if the account is on the Free plan with no edge rule in front, which the source cannot confirm.
claimed_root_cause: The only request controls are per-network counters (the RL_IP binding and the D1 sign-in buckets keyed by IPv4 address or IPv6 /64), checked inside the Worker after the invocation is already counted. No global or aggregate cap protects the shared daily request and D1 rows-written allowances that both deployments rely on during a timed test.

trace.description: Every anonymous /api/ request enters the Worker and reaches requestGuard; the invocation, and its use of the daily request allowance, has already happened before any limit is checked.

The RL_IP ceiling is keyed by clientNetwork(request) (CF-Connecting-IP reduced to IPv4 address or IPv6 /64): 3000 per 60 s (wrangler.toml:42, 152). It fails open (line 308), and a refused request still returns from inside the Worker.
An unauthenticated sign-in with an email not on the list calls candidateUnknownEmail, after one D1 read in candidateSigninPaused (line 43).
Counts the attempt against the per-network bucket cand-ip:<hash(network)> with limit CANDIDATE_UNKNOWN_PER_IP=200 (line 47) per 10-minute window, then pauses that network only.
IPv6 is grouped by /64, so each /64 a client controls starts a fresh bucket with its own 200-attempt allowance and a new rate_limits row.

INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING on rate_limits: at least one D1 row written per counted unauthenticated attempt, charged to the account-wide daily rows-written allowance that candidate answer saves and heartbeats on both sites also use.

evidence.description: The project's budget lists 'Requests: 100,000 a day' (Free plan, per account) with 100 writers candidates using about 18%.
The budget lists 'D1 rows written: 100,000 a day' with 100 writers candidates using about 35%.
'Both sites share the account's daily limits'; 100 support plus 100 writers candidates come to about 95,000 rows written; limits reset at 00:00 UTC.
The Cloudflare plan is recorded as an open question ('Which Cloudflare plan is the account on?').
Support RL_IP simple = { limit = 3000, period = 60 } per network, about 4.3M requests a day per network, far above the account's daily request allowance.
Writers RL_IP has the same 3000 per 60 s per-network limit in its own namespace.
The writers configuration is tuned to 'stay inside the Workers Free limits', indicating the Free plan is the deployment target.
CANDIDATE_UNKNOWN_PER_IP = 200: each network may cause 200 counted D1 upserts per 10-minute window before it is paused. The bound is per network only.
clientIp uses CF-Connecting-IP, so the per-network key is the real client address; rotation requires controlling many addresses or /64s.
The per-request limiter fails open by design, so it cannot act as a hard aggregate cap.
The writers site uses the same unknown-email counter, so both deployments add to the shared account allowances.

blockers: The Cloudflare plan for the account hosting talo and talo-docs (Free or Workers Paid) is not visible in source and decides whether the shared daily allowances exist at all.

Whether any zone-level WAF or rate-limiting rule, or custom domain with such a rule, sits in front of the workers.dev hostnames (and so stops traffic before the Worker is invoked) is deployment state outside the repository.
How many D1 rows written one rate_limits upsert costs (table row plus the TEXT PRIMARY KEY autoindex) needs a local measurement.
No OS-enforced sandbox for target execution in this run, so the local measurement was not performed.

validation_plan.local: Add a vitest case in test/ (workerd pool, migrate() and req() from test/helpers.ts, RL_* bindings unset as in the existing tests, CF-Connecting-IP set per request as in test/ratelimit-parse.test.ts). For N = 1..5, send 210 POST /api/candidate/login requests with distinct unlisted emails (x<N>-<i>@example.test) and CF-Connecting-IP 2001:db8:0:N::1. Assert: responses 1-199 per network are 403, response 200 is 429, responses 201-210 are 429; SELECT bucket, count FROM rate_limits WHERE bucket LIKE 'cand-ip:%' returns exactly 5 rows each with count = 200 (1,000 counted writes in total, growing linearly with networks and with no aggregate cap). Separately, run the countStmt SQL text with .run() on a fresh bucket and on an existing bucket and record meta.rows_written for each to measure the rows-written cost per attempt. No external calls or paid services are involved.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner checks the account's plan in the Cloudflare dashboard (Workers & Pages > Plans) and whether any WAF rate-limiting rule or custom domain fronts the talo and talo-docs Workers. If the account is on the Free plan, the owner reviews the Workers and D1 usage graphs for the requests and rows-written baseline of a normal drive. Do not generate load against production. If the account is Free and nothing fronts the Workers, mitigations are moving to Workers Paid or adding an edge rate-limiting rule (which runs before the Worker) for /api/candidate/login and /api/admin/login.

title: Bootstrap admin sessions stay valid after ADMIN_PASSWORD/PANEL_PASSWORD rotation or bootstrap email removal
description: The config-credential (bootstrap) manager and panel logins create sessions with user_id NULL. For those sessions getAdminRole returns the role embedded in the signed token and never checks that the bootstrap credential that issued them still exists or is unchanged. Rotating ADMIN_PASSWORD or PANEL_PASSWORD (wrangler secret put), or blanking ADMIN_EMAIL/PANEL_EMAIL to disable the login, therefore leaves every bootstrap session minted before the change valid until its 12-hour expiry. Only rotating SESSION_SECRET ends them, and that also invalidates every candidate session, including candidates in the middle of a timed test, because candidate sessions are stateless HMAC tokens. Named accounts have their sessions revoked on password change, deactivation and delete. Bootstrap sessions have no equivalent control, and no admin action can end another bootstrap session (logout deletes only the caller's own token). The exposure is limited to sessions that already existed before the rotation: after rotation the old password can no longer mint new sessions. During that window, whoever holds a pre-rotation bootstrap manager session (for example someone who signed in with a leaked or former password, or holds a copied cookie) keeps full manager authority. That includes POST /api/admin/members with role 'manager', which creates a durable named manager account that outlives the 12h session. That account does appear in the Access list and in the audit log as member_add.
claimed_root_cause: Session validity for user_id-NULL (bootstrap) sessions depends only on the HMAC signature under SESSION_SECRET and on an unexpired admin_sessions row (src/lib/auth.ts:176-189, 195). The session is not bound to the bootstrap credential that issued it (createAdminSession signs {admin, role, iat} and stores user_id NULL, auth.ts:159-163), and nothing deletes user_id IS NULL rows when that credential changes.

trace.description: An anonymous caller gets the bootstrap manager login when loginEmail === ADMIN_EMAIL and timingSafeEqual(pass, ADMIN_PASSWORD). The panel bootstrap is at L255. Both run only after the named-account check (L247) fails.
createAdminSession(env, loginRole, loginUserId) is called with loginUserId still null (initialised at L233) for bootstrap logins.
The token payload is {admin:true, role, iat}, signed with SESSION_SECRET, and the row is inserted with user_id NULL and a 12h expires_at (L160-163). No credential identifier or version is recorded.
Each later request verifies the HMAC (L176) and then looks up the session by token and expiry only (L182-189). The LEFT JOIN to admin_users gives null columns for a bootstrap row.

For user_id NULL the token's role is returned ('manager' unless it says 'member'). ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PASSWORD, PANEL_EMAIL and PANEL_PASSWORD are never consulted, so admin.ts:272 still accepts a session minted before a rotation as manager.

evidence.description: Sibling control: a named account's sessions are revoked on password change or deactivation, and on delete at L462. Its role and active flag are also re-read on every request (auth.ts:190-194). Bootstrap sessions have no equivalent.
revokeUserSessions deletes only WHERE user_id = ?, so it never matches a bootstrap session (user_id NULL).

Besides per-token logout (auth.ts:84), the only other admin_sessions deletion in the support retention job is the expiry purge. The writers retention job has the same expiry-only purge at src/routes/admin-docs.ts:564. No code removes live user_id IS NULL rows.
A manager session can create a named account with role 'manager' (members POST, L435-453; gated only by role === 'manager' at L436). This turns the 12h window into durable manager access.
Candidate sessions are stateless HMAC tokens under the same SESSION_SECRET, so the only way to end bootstrap admin sessions (rotating SESSION_SECRET) also logs out every candidate.
The documented credential setup (npx wrangler secret put ADMIN_PASSWORD) says nothing about ending existing admin sessions. docs/WRITERS-SITE.md:52 has the same gap for the writers site.

blockers: No OS-enforced sandbox for target execution in this run, so the old session being accepted after credential rotation could not be observed locally (source predicts 200 with role 'manager').

validation_plan.local: Add a vitest case to test/security-fixes.test.ts. Import worker from '../src/index' and env, createExecutionContext and waitOnExecutionContext from 'cloudflare:test', following the pattern in test/audit-round3.test.ts:255-258. In beforeEach run migrate(), then const mgr = await adminCookie() (bootstrap admin@test.local / 'test-admin-pass' from vitest.config.ts). Define call(e, path, init) = worker.fetch(new Request('https://test.local' + path, init), e, ctx) followed by waitOnExecutionContext(ctx). (1) With rotated = { ...env, ADMIN_PASSWORD: 'rotated-pass' }, GET /api/admin/config with Cookie mgr. Intended: 401. Source predicts 200 with body.role === 'manager'. (2) Repeat with { ...env, ADMIN_EMAIL: '' }. (3) With rotated, POST /api/admin/members with headers Cookie mgr, Origin https://test.local, Content-Type application/json and body {"name":"x","email":"x@test.local","password":"0123456789","role":"manager"}. Intended: 401. Source predicts 200 and a new admin_users row with role 'manager'. (4) Repeat (1) for panelCookie() with { ...env, PANEL_PASSWORD: 'rotated-panel' }. Source predicts 200 with role 'member'. Control: create a named account, sign in, reset its password through POST /api/admin/members/:id and confirm its old cookie already returns 401. All fixture data is test-local, and the test D1 is reset between cases.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed only, with no audit traffic. (a) Confirm whether the team's credential-rotation or offboarding procedure for ADMIN_PASSWORD/PANEL_PASSWORD (support and docs environments) also rotates SESSION_SECRET or clears admin_sessions. The repository does not document either step. (b) Run a read-only count of live bootstrap sessions on each database: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM admin_sessions WHERE user_id IS NULL AND expires_at > strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','now'). (c) Optionally, on a staging copy only: sign in with the bootstrap manager login, rotate ADMIN_PASSWORD with wrangler secret put, and check whether the same browser session still loads /api/admin/config as manager.
